title: Mortifying Sin
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Mortifying sin means putting sin to death by the power of the Holy Spirit. Believers are not called to excuse, hide, manage, or make peace with sin, but to fight it through repentance, truth, faith, and dependence on God.
summary: Mortifying sin means putting sin to death by the power of the Holy Spirit. Believers are not called to excuse, hide, manage, or make peace with sin, but to fight it through repentance, truth, faith, and dependence on God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ died not only to forgive sin, but to break its dominion over His people. Because believers belong to the crucified and risen Christ, they are called to put to death what belongs to the old life and walk in newness of life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sin is not a harmless weakness to be entertained. Scripture calls believers to put sin to death. This means taking sin seriously because it dishonors God, damages the soul, harms others, and wars against the life of faith.

Mortifying sin is not the same as trying harder in human strength. Paul teaches that believers put sin to death by the Spirit. The same Spirit who gives life also empowers God’s people to resist the flesh, confess sin, reject temptation, and walk in obedience.

This doctrine is rooted in union with Christ. The old self was crucified with Him, and believers are no longer slaves of sin. Sin may still tempt, deceive, and attack, but it no longer has rightful dominion over those who belong to Jesus.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people either minimize sin or become crushed by it. Some excuse sin as personality, struggle, trauma, weakness, or habit. Others believe repeated temptation means change is impossible.

This doctrine is especially important for believers battling addiction, lust, bitterness, anger, fear, pride, envy, or secret sin. Christ does not call His people to manage chains He died to break.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Name sin honestly before God and refuse to make peace with it. Bring it into the light, confess it, remove what feeds it, and depend on the Holy Spirit to put it to death. Stand in Christ’s victory, use Scripture, pray, seek faithful accountability, and pursue obedience one step at a time.
